 Nutson's Weekly Auto News Wrapup October 25, 2026
 The Auto Channel — Trusted automotive reporting for 32 years. This article is part of The Auto Channel’s independent automotive coverage library — one of the longest-running automotive publications online (since 1995). Our editors test, research, 
and document vehicles, technologies, recalls, and ownership experiences to help drivers make informed decisions.
 Unlike short news blurbs, our content is written for long-term usefulness — explaining what the vehicle is, why it matters, and how it affects real owners.
 Coverage includes reviews, specifications, safety data, recall history, industry context, and real-world driving impressions collected over decades of reporting.
 Larry Nutson 
AUTO CENTRAL – Louisville, KY: October 25, 2026; Every Sunday for over 30 years, 
 Larry Nutson - The Chicago Car Guy and Executive 
Producer of The Auto Channel - has delivered his weekly take on the automotive world. Each report distills the week’s top stories into sharp, easy-to-digest News Nuggets.
The full version of today’s News Nuggets — along with hundreds of thousands of additional articles, reviews, and editorial insights — can be found in The Auto Channel’s Million-Page Automotive 
Library, built and indexed over three decades. To dive deeper, simply copy any headline and paste it into this or any Site Search box on The Auto Channel. 
 LEARN MORE FROM THE WEB'S LONGEST RUNNING AUTOMOTIVE COLUMN 
 Here are Larry's Top Auto Story Picks of the Week of October 19 - October 24, 2026. Larry picked these as important, relevant, interesting, and sometimes semi-secret stories you need to know - served up 
as snappy, opinionated, and insider-sharp. These are expertly crafted, easy-to-understand news nuggets that cut through the noise and get right to what matters to you in the automotive world.
 * Rivian on the move. Rivian outsold every EV brand except Tesla in the US during Q3 2026, jumping from sixth place in Q2 to second, according to the corrected sales report Cox Automotive published with Kelley Blue Book. 
Rivian's estimated 19,239 sales put it about 6,300 units ahead of Toyota at 12,904, with Cadillac at 12,358 and Hyundai at 12,185 right behind. Chevrolet, which led every non-Tesla brand in Q2 with 14,908, fell to 10,031. Three 
months ago Rivian's 11,405 sales trailed Chevrolet, Hyundai, Cadillac and Toyota.
 * EV road trip down south. Readers challenged Wall Street Journal columnist Christopher Mims to take an affordable electric car on a route with less-than-ideal charging options. 
 Click to read what happened .
 * BTW. AAA reports the average price for regular gas is $4.29, up from $3.06 a year ago. Diesel is $6.35, up from $3.66. 
 See it here .
 * Fun cars from Ford for Europe. Ford Europe President Jim Baumbick is leading a comeback plan to sell new racing-inspired, hybrid and electric vehicles by the end of the decade. The automaker's sales in Europe declined 
36% over the last decade, squeezed by Chinese competition. Ford's upcoming vehicles are years away, with two small electric cars not going on sale until 2028 and three new SUVs arriving in 2029. Will this spill over to the US? 
Who knows! 
 Learn more here .
 * See where the cameras are. MapQuest has made an update to its software and will now show you where license plate readers such as Flock cameras and others are in your neighborhood. You can see the locations of known 
outdoor surveillance cameras in the app. 
 More here from Engadget .
 * MotorTrend CoTY. Mercedes-Benz S-Class is the 2027 MotorTrend Car of the Year. With a new engine, a new operating system, hands-free driving, and plenty of opulence, this flagship sets an industry standard. Every 
year, the MotorTrend team invites a field of new and significantly updated vehicles to vie for its prestigious Car of the Year award. The 2027 field of competitors comprised 22 cars spanning a wide range of segments. A team of 
expert judges rigorously evaluates each vehicle against six key criteria – advancement in design, engineering excellence, performance of intended function, value, safety and efficiency – to determine the car most 
worthy of the iconic "Golden Calipers" trophy. 
 Read more from Motor Trend here .
 * About younger car collectors. Baby boomers embraced brawny cars from the 1950s and '60s, but as new collectors take up the hobby, Mazdas and Nissans from the 1980s and '90s are hot, and still don't break the bank. 
Later generations are entering their peak earning years, and with cash to spend on a hobby, they have their own ideas about what defines a classic car. 
 Give a read here .
 * Ford recall. Ford Motor Co. is recalling 102,159 F-Series trucks in the United States over faulty equipment, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration said. The analog tachometer, which shows engine speed 
in revolutions per minute, and speedometer may get stuck or move erratically and provide inaccurate readings, NHTSA said. The recall covers certain 2025-2026 F-250 SD, F-350 SD, F-450 SD, F-550 SD, F-600, and 2026 F-150 and 
F-750 SD trucks.
 * Volkswagen recall. The Volkswagen ID.4 was recalled over a fire risk stemming from the car's high-voltage battery. VW says that the cause is still unknown. Owners are being asked not to charge above 80%—and 
unless they opt out by next week, VW will automatically limit their cars to 80% charge.
 * Toyota recall. Toyota is recalling 105,794 model-year 2024–2027 Land Cruiser Hybrid vehicles in the U.S. due to a faulty fuel tube connection near the gas tank that can disconnect and leak fuel, creating 
a fire risk.
 * Land Rover recall. Jaguar Land Rover will recall 93,997 vehicles in the United States as the rearview camera image "may fail to appear on the display", the US National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) 
said. NHTSA said insufficient drain holes may trap water in the rearview camera and damage it. The recall affects certain 2022-2026 Land Rover Range Rover vehicles, according to the auto safety regulator.
 * 2026 Rebelle Rally. After a week of challenging navigation and driving across 2,600+ kilometers, Rebelle Rally proudly introduced this year's podium finishers! First in the 4x4 class is Team #188 Teralin Petereit 
and Laura Wanlass, piloting a 2025 Ford Ranger Raptor. Subaru took another win at the Rebelle Rally in the X-Cross class with Team #200 6x Rebelle Carey Lando and 10x Rebelle Andrea Shaffer driving a 2025 Subaru Forester Hybrid.
* NASCAR Manufacturer Champ. Toyota clinched the 2026 NASCAR Cup Series Manufacturers' Championship, breaking a seven-year drought to win its fourth manufacturer title. For the last five years, Chevrolet has been the 
champ. The overall 2026 Cup Series Driver's Championship is still undecided as the season approaches its final races. 
 More race news here. .
 * IndyCar to race in Spain. Penske Entertainment and Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya have confirmed the IndyCar Series will pay its first visit to the Spanish road course next summer. The inaugural IndyCar Grand 
Prix of Barcelona is set for July 16-18 at the venue that hosts everything from Formula 1 to MotoGP to the World Endurance Championship and will serve as a homecoming race for reigning IndyCar champion Alex Palou of Chip 
Ganassi Racing. The multi-year agreement will give IndyCar its first international anchor since its trips to race around Brazil's Sambadrome in Sao Paulo from 2010-13.
 * A decade of driver development. Mercedes Formula 1 driver Kimi Antonelli is on the verge of becoming the youngest champion in the sport's history. Mercedes spent seven years and $10 million developing Antonelli 
after spotting him as an 11-year-old go-kart racer. Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff chose to stick with Antonelli through a rookie season that included both brilliant moments and mistakes. And today, Sunday, October 25, is race day! 
 Read more here 
 Stay safe. Be Well.
 Kind regards, 
Larry Nutson, the Chicago Car Guy
